questions.stem: Under the crewing rules, when must a vessel on a voyage have a chief mate?
options: When it is over 15 gross tonnage on any voyage
When it makes any voyage at all outside sheltered waters
At 500 GT or more, or with more than 50 passengers
When it carries more than 12 passengers on board
questions.explanation: Section 212(4)(b) sets two triggers: 500 GT or more, or more than 50 passengers. The 15 GT and 12 passenger figures belong to the inspection-certificate and Small Vessel Regulations tests, not this one.

questions.stem: The crewing rules in Division 2 of Part 2 of the Marine Personnel Regulations apply to which vessels?
options: Only Canadian vessels over 500 gross tonnage
Only foreign vessels in Canadian waters
Self-propelled Canadian vessels engaged on a voyage
Only Canadian vessels that carry passengers for hire
questions.explanation: Section 200(1) applies Division 2 to self-propelled Canadian vessels on a voyage. Foreign vessels in Canadian waters are covered by Division 4.

questions.stem: Who may act as a member of the deck watch?
options: Only the master, or a person holding a master's certificate
A person certificated as appropriate to the vessel's class, area and duties
Any adult crew member the master chooses for the watch
Only a person holding an Able Seafarer certificate, at any tonnage
questions.explanation: Section 214 sets the test as an appropriate certificate for vessel class, area and duties, and also stops the master from permitting anything else. Able Seafarer is a minimum only for the additional person at 500 GT and above.

questions.stem: A 12 GT passenger vessel is under way with a VHF radiotelephone installed. What must the person in charge of the deck watch hold?
options: Only a certificate of competency; the radio operator certificate is optional
A Bridge Watch Rating certificate and a pleasure craft card
Only a radio operator certificate for the VHF on board
A watchkeeping certificate and a suitable radio operator certificate
questions.explanation: Section 216(2)(a) requires a certificate authorizing watchkeeping and radio watch duties and, if there is a VHF radiotelephone, a suitable radio operator certificate. Bridge Watch Rating is the rating-level certificate for the additional person at 500 GT and above.

questions.stem: At what size must a deck watch include an additional person, and what must that person hold at 500 gross tonnage or more?
options: 5 GT or more; a Bridge Watch Rating certificate at every size
500 GT or more; an Able Seafarer certificate only
15 GT or more; at 150 GT or more a Master's certificate
5 GT or more; at 500 GT or more, at least Able Seafarer or Bridge Watch Rating
questions.explanation: Section 216(2)(b) requires the additional person from 5 GT, and sets the AB or BWR certificate as the minimum only when the vessel is 500 GT or more. Below 500 GT the person does not need that certificate.

questions.stem: A 7 GT sightseeing boat has an unobstructed all-round view from the steering position and makes a 4 nautical mile loop within harbour limits in good visibility at 1400 on a clear August day. Is an additional person required in the deck watch?
options: Yes, because the trip is more than 2 nautical miles
No, but only because the trip is under one hour
No, all the conditions of the s. 216(3) exception are met
Yes, any vessel of 5 GT or more must always have an additional person
questions.explanation: Section 216(3)(b) excuses a vessel up to 500 GT with an unobstructed all-round view from the steering position on a voyage of not more than 5 nautical miles within harbour limits, in good visibility between sunrise and sunset. All are satisfied. Trip duration is not a condition.

questions.stem: The same 7 GT boat takes the same 4 nautical mile loop in good visibility at 2130 in October, after sunset. Is an additional person required?
options: No, the exception applies at any time of day in good visibility
Yes, but only if there are more than 12 passengers
Yes, the exception only applies between sunrise and sunset
No, because the trip is under 5 nautical miles
questions.explanation: The s. 216(3)(b) exception requires all of its conditions together, including that the voyage takes place between sunrise and sunset. After dark the exception does not apply, so the 5 GT rule applies.

questions.stem: When is the master counted as a member of the deck watch?
options: Only when the master holds a Master Mariner certificate
Only when the vessel is under 5 GT and in sheltered waters
Never; the master is always in addition to the deck watch
At anchor or moored, at not more than 1 000 GT, or 1 000 to 3 000 GT with three watches
questions.explanation: Section 215(2) lists those three cases. On a small BC vessel the master is therefore counted as part of the watch.

questions.stem: What is a Safe Manning Document and which vessels need one under s. 202(3)(b)?
options: A document issued by the owner each season stating the number of persons carried on each voyage
A Minister's document for certain inspected vessels listing the minimum crew and certificates
A permit allowing a vessel to operate with an uncertificated master for 6 months
A certificate issued to each crew member showing they have completed MED training
questions.explanation: That is what s. 202(3)(b) and (5) describe, and it must be carried on board. The 6-month item is a dispensation under s. 204, which is a different thing.

questions.stem: A harbour tug is assisting another vessel while attached to it by a tow line. Does the deck watch rule require an additional person?
options: Yes, but only after sunset or when visibility is restricted
Yes, always, because the tug is 5 GT or more
No, but only if the tug has a working radar
No, a tug attached to the vessel by a tow line is excused
questions.explanation: Section 216(3)(c) lists a tug assisting another vessel while attached to it by a tow line as an exception. Radar and time of day are not part of that exception.

questions.stem: What does s. 213 require of the master about planning and the deck watch?
options: Ensure every deck watch member holds a master's certificate
Plan the voyage and keep a deck watch as the STCW Code A-VIII/2 requires
Ensure the voyage plan is approved by Transport Canada before departure
Ensure the voyage is planned only if the vessel exceeds 500 gross tonnage
questions.explanation: Section 213 ties the master's planning and watch duty to the watchkeeping parts of the STCW Code. It does not require approval by Transport Canada or limit the duty by tonnage.
